is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles gambiae s.s. (Page 1, 2).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study reports genotyping for kdr East (Vgsc L1014S) and kdr West (Vgsc L1014F) (Page 2, 9, 14).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: The paper reports that 100 mosquitoes (50 resistant and 50 susceptible) were genotyped, finding that kdr East was nearly fixed (99% or 99.14%) and kdr West was present in 1% of samples (Page 2, 14, 20).

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected as blood-fed/gravid females from Tulukuyi village, Bungoma County, Kenya in 2018, and their F1 progeny were used (Page 2, 6).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical study characterizing the microbiota and insecticide resistance markers of field-collected mosquitoes.

sub_country_location.evidence: Data is tied to Tulukuyi village, Bungoma County, Kenya (0.56°N 34.56°E) (Page 6).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Collections were conducted in April and May 2018 (Page 6).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study appears to be an independent investigation of mosquito microbiota by researchers from KEMRI and CDC, using specific 2018 collections.

supplement.evidence: The genotype frequencies are summarized in the main text as being fixed or nearly fixed (99%), which is sufficient for extraction.

assessment.summary: This study characterizes the microbiota of Anopheles gambiae s.s. from Tulukuyi village, Bungoma County, Western Kenya, in relation to permethrin resistance. F1 progeny of field-caught mosquitoes were tested using CDC bottle bioassays (5X dose). A subset of 100 mosquitoes (50 resistant and 50 susceptible) were genotyped for kdr mutations. The kdr East (L1014S) mutation was found to be nearly fixed (99-99.14%) in the population, while kdr West (L1014F) was detected in 1% of the samples.
